reviews.title: The BEST completely CUSTOMIZABLE way to take power back from your phone!!
reviews.text: No matter what you could possibly want to do with a screen control app, ScreenZen has either already implemented it or is actively working towards making it a reality. The developer is clearly putting people first and creating an AMAZING product for us to stop the phone addiction without losing any functionality from our phones. There are levels to how strict you want the app to block you from your apps, up to the same strictness as a Brick (which I also have, but have many issues with forgetting to unbrick for certain scenarios). I also love how you can block yourself based on whether you have hit your personal limits for the day, not just by schedule or on demand (although you can do that too). They’ve also introduced a minimal version of many social media apps, so that you can customize even your experience within the apps (taking away explore feeds, stories, home feeds, etc). reviews.title: Reclaiming my time
reviews.text:
This app has been central to regaining time lost to social media. The prompts to pause 10 seconds and ask “why am I opening this app” have been most helpful. Instead of opening an app every time I have a few minutes (and having those few minutes turn into an hour or more of scrolling) that pause prior to opening has helped me to just sit and be present. It’s ok to have a few unfilled moments in your day!  You don’t need an app for that!

Being off social media more has meant that I don’t get bogged down and drawn into every silly drama I scroll over. I worry less about things outside my control (social media is so good at bringing other people’s problems into your space!) and spend more time present in my own sphere of influence. My head is clearer. I have reclaimed my wasted time and can use it in more important things. And not one of my friends has complained that they haven’t seen pictures of my meals or my vacations or that I haven’t shared some political post or AI generated heartfelt fake story lately. 

This app is life changing if you’re ready for that. You have control of which apps to limit, how long you spend on each (I allow myself 3-10 minute sessions a day on FB and Instagram, and rarely use those three sessions), and set a 10 second delay to open them which is usually enough time to decide I don’t really need to open them. 

There is a period of “withdrawal” you need to work through. Recognize that replacing one bad habit with another (apps you don’t have limited) is a temptation you must avoid. Have a plan for the time you’ll save - make a to-do list - or plan to personally reach out to a friend instead of “connecting” by liking their post.  This app is a tool - it’s not magic. You have to do some work, too. But you’ll be so glad you did!
